method: Public-source research and bounded link checks. No calls, applications, personal outcomes or live inventory checks. Provider reports are attributed; a recognized provider is not a guarantee of current access.

reviews.finding: CHOMP’s 2025 assessment, page 146, reports providing lab work and diagnostic testing to RotaCare Monterey patients. This independently documents care delivered; the clinic page supplies the current appointment route.
reviews.limits: Appointment availability and suitability for an individual were not confirmed.

reviews.finding: 211 independently lists CHS outpatient assessments, counseling, Medi-Cal and sliding fees. The provider and directory agree on the Salinas assessment phone. This supports a real treatment service, not a measured recovery-success claim.
reviews.limits: No treatment slot, clinical outcome, or individual coverage decision was confirmed.

reviews.finding: The City of Gonzales independently identifies CCES energy-bill assistance and the same application phone. The provider FAQ confirms required documents and the application process.
reviews.limits: Current funds and approval for any particular household were not confirmed.

reviews.finding: The City of Gonzales and CCES describe weatherization for eligible owners and renters. The provider confirms that renters also need the owner’s agreement.
reviews.limits: No assessment appointment, installed measure or individual energy saving was confirmed.

reviews.finding: California’s Department of Aging lists Alliance on Aging as Monterey County’s HICAP provider. The provider confirms free counseling and the program phone; its unfinished online appointment page is not used.
reviews.limits: Appointment openings and individual insurance savings were not confirmed.

reviews.finding: County records document a 2025–26 meals contract. The current provider page describes home delivery and intake. The old contract is historical corroboration, not proof of current funding or an available delivery route.
reviews.limits: Current enrollment, route coverage and a start date must be confirmed with the program.

reviews.finding: California’s Department of Aging includes Meals on Wheels Salinas in its 2025 nutrition-program stories. The provider currently publishes home-delivery eligibility and intake. Testimonials are not an independent effectiveness study.
reviews.limits: Enrollment and the first delivery date were not confirmed.

reviews.finding: Monterey County Bar Foundation identifies Legal Services for Seniors as a 2025 grant recipient providing free help to county residents age 60+. The provider confirms services and intake phone.
reviews.limits: Case acceptance, appointment availability and legal results were not confirmed.

reviews.finding: California Department of Education’s indexed resource-and-referral listing matches the provider and 831-757-0775. Direct CDE retrieval was blocked; the current provider page confirms that families receive options and must contact each childcare provider about space.
reviews.limits: A referral does not secure childcare, a subsidy, or a vacant place.

reviews.finding: 211 independently lists CCCIL assistive-technology services. A fresh provider-page fetch confirms the program and 831-757-2968. This documents assessment/device assistance, not guaranteed free equipment.
reviews.limits: Device inventory, suitability, cost and loan eligibility were not confirmed.

reviews.finding: The Workforce Development Board’s 2024 impact report describes job-search, training and placement support. The current service-center page supplies the contact route. The report is provider-published, not an independent job-outcome evaluation.
reviews.limits: Enrollment and any particular job or training placement were not confirmed.

reviews.finding: The City of Santa Cruz’s November 2025 statement independently recognizes Second Harvest’s food-distribution role. The current foodbank page lists its food hotline and locator. The historical funding pledge is not treated as current available funds.
reviews.limits: A hotline referral does not confirm food stock or pickup access at a specific site.

reviews.finding: City recognition corroborates Second Harvest as a local food provider; its current CalFresh page documents application help and the hotline. Foodbank assistance is separate from the county’s benefit decision.
reviews.limits: Individual eligibility, benefit amount and approval were not confirmed.

reviews.finding: Second Harvest is independently recognized by the city. Its diaper page identifies public distribution partners separately from partners serving enrolled clients. The card links to the public list.
reviews.limits: Diaper stock, sizes, hours and each partner’s intake conditions were not confirmed.

reviews.finding: The California State Bar’s 2026 legal-aid grant recipient list includes Watsonville Law Center. Its contact page documents public intake instructions and limited availability. Business and existing-client numbers are not presented as new-client intake.
reviews.limits: No case acceptance, legal outcome or immediate appointment was confirmed.

reviews.finding: The county’s indexed housing-program page identifies its ECHO counseling arrangement. Direct county retrieval was blocked. ECHO’s current page lists Monterey-area tenant/landlord counseling, mediation and the county phone.
reviews.limits: This is counseling/referral; no rent payment, legal representation or dispute outcome is promised.

reviews.finding: The SPCA’s 2025 report states that its Pet Food Bank distributed 152,180 pounds of food. This is a provider-reported delivery total. The current recipient page specifically says critical need and confirms Saturday pickup and limits.
reviews.limits: Current stock and food types were not confirmed. This is help during critical need, not a stock-up offer.

reviews.finding: A San Benito County-hosted ADRC directory independently recognizes Del Mar and its service region. That directory is historical; the current provider page supplies eligibility, contact and support options.
reviews.limits: Respite funds, copays and appointment openings must be confirmed. No caregiver health outcome is guaranteed.

reviews.finding: MST’s published FY2025 figures report 186,167 RIDES passenger trips. Its current ADA page documents eligibility and the application process. Trips are not a count of unique people or proof of availability for a requested journey.
reviews.limits: Individual eligibility, service corridor and advance booking must be confirmed.

reviews.finding: The city library is a real public service, but its old adult-learning deep link returned 404 on a fresh request. Its replacement city page does not substantiate the specific tutoring waitlist and access details in this card.
reviews.limits: Held from Ready until current tutoring instructions are confirmed.

reviews.finding: United Way’s 2025 annual report documents 12,308 phone/text contacts and approximately 18,750 referrals. Its two referral totals differ slightly, so no exact referral total is repeated. Referrals are not confirmed successful assistance.
reviews.limits: No promise that a referred agency has space, funding or accepts a particular applicant.

reviews.finding: MST is the public transit district. Its current travel-training page documents free instruction in planning and taking bus trips. System ridership does not establish a specific training-completion or independence outcome.
reviews.limits: A training appointment or personal outcome was not confirmed.

reviews.finding: The city confirms the library system, but the old computers/Wi-Fi deep link returned 404 on a fresh request. Current guest-pass and session-length rules have not been re-established from the replacement page.
reviews.limits: Held from Ready until current computer-access instructions are confirmed.

reviews.finding: The city confirms the library system, but the old Wi-Fi details page returned 404 on a fresh request. The replacement page does not establish the advertised 8 a.m.–8 p.m. access window.
reviews.limits: Held from Ready until the current Wi-Fi access window is confirmed.

reviews.finding: The police website identifies Salinas Connect as the city-service channel. Its linked portal returned 404 in fresh requests while the web index still showed an older portal page; the current submission route is unresolved.
reviews.limits: Held from Ready until the service-request destination loads successfully. No request was submitted.

reviews.finding: MST’s official district website links its service-alerts page. This is an operational information tool for riders, not a benefit or a guarantee that every disruption has been posted.
reviews.limits: Check the live route information before traveling; no service availability or all-clear is promised.

reviews.finding: The county’s indexed food-resource page recognizes this Food Bank. The current provider schedule explicitly lists 11/5/26, 9–10 a.m., Our Lady of Refuge, 11140 Preston Street. The fresh HTML and web reader agree; stale 2024 rows were excluded.
reviews.limits: Pickup operation and stock were not confirmed directly. This card expires at the listed event end.

reviews.finding: The county’s indexed food-resource page recognizes this Food Bank. The current provider schedule explicitly lists 11/6/26, 9–10 a.m., St. Philip’s, 8065 Carmel Valley Road, for seniors and the general public. Old-year rows were excluded.
reviews.limits: Pickup operation and stock were not confirmed directly. This card expires at the listed event end.
